transcript.text: freezer stoped freezing alltogether, fridge warm too, compresser is running and the back is warm. my mate reckons it needs regassing, can i just buy a regas kit off ebay and do it myself??

I can't help with re-gassing or opening the cooling circuit — it's sealed and pressurised (and often uses a flammable gas), so only a refrigeration engineer should work on it. Please don't pierce or cut any pipes. No, please don't. Working on the refrigerant circuit needs specialist equipment and an F-gas qualified engineer, and many modern fridge-freezers use a flammable refrigerant, so DIY kits are a real safety risk. From what you have described, the most likely cause is the sealed cooling system or its controls. Is the freezer still cold while the fridge is warm, and is there a thick block of ice on the back wall inside the freezer?
freezer isnt cold at all, about 0C and everything has thawed, fridge about 13C. no ice or frost on the back wall, its not even cold. compressor just runs non stop tho

Fridge freezers lose their heat through a coil or grille at the back or underneath. Gently dust or vacuum it, and leave a few centimetres of space between it and the wall or cupboards. Was it dusty or pushed against the wall (and have you sorted it), or was it already clean with space round it?
not sure, i havent looked at it properly. the back is only barely warm tho, not hot like it used to be. can i fix this myself or not?

It depends on what the cause turns out to be. Problems like a faulty door seal, dusty coils or too little space around it are usually safe to sort yourself. From what you have described, the most likely cause is dusty coils or too little space round it. Run your fingers round the rubber door seal on each door and look for splits, gaps or a section that has come away, or anything stopping it closing flat. Is the seal torn or come away, was it dirty or folded (and is that sorted), or does it look fine?
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]

not checked the seal yet, and i cant really tell by looking. you still havent said if i can fix it myself tho. the sticker inside says R600a if that matters, and i chipped ice out of the freezer with a knife a few months back

Probably not, if the fault turns out to be in the sealed cooling system. That system holds R600a, a flammable gas, so any regassing or pipe repair must be done by a qualified refrigeration engineer, not at home. From what you have described, the most likely cause is the sealed cooling system or its controls. Keep both doors shut for about 24 hours (only open them briefly) and let it recover. After a day with the doors shut, is it back to cold, or still warm?
